title: Serbia-Montenegro

endonym.native: Државна заједница Србија и Црна Гора

capsule: The State Union of Serbia and Montenegro (Državna zajednica Srbija i Crna Gora) was established in February 2003 as the successor to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, following the Belgrade Agreement brokered by the EU, and comprised two constituent republics sharing defense and foreign-affairs institutions while maintaining separate economies, currencies, and customs regimes. The union's constitutional charter allowed either republic to hold an independence referendum after three years, and Montenegro exercised that right in May 2006; the referendum exceeded the required 55 % threshold by a narrow margin (55.5 %), and Montenegro declared independence on 3 June 2006, dissolving the union. Serbia immediately succeeded to international legal personality, including UN membership, while Montenegro applied separately.
